title: Pemphigus Vulgaris vs Bullous Pemphigoid vs Dermatitis Herpetiformis
subtitle: Key distinguishing features for differential diagnosis

values.pv: 40–60 y; M = F; higher prevalence in Ashkenazi Jewish and Mediterranean populations
values.bp: >70 y; M slightly > F; drug triggers (DPP-4 inhibitors, checkpoint inhibitors, furosemide); associated neurological disease (dementia, Parkinson's)
values.dh: Young adults (20–40 y); M > F; Northern European; strongly associated with celiac disease (HLA-DQ2/DQ8)

values.pv: Flaccid, easily ruptured blisters; Nikolsky sign positive (lateral pressure extends blister); crusted erosions common; oral erosions may precede skin disease
values.bp: Tense, intact blisters on urticarial, erythematous, or eczematous base; Nikolsky sign negative; intense pruritus; lower trunk and flexures
values.dh: Grouped, intensely pruritic vesicles on extensor surfaces (elbows, knees, scalp, buttocks); often excoriated before reaching clinical assessment; vesicles not tense

values.pv: Typical — often the FIRST sign; oral erosions in >90%; nasal, pharyngeal, genital, conjunctival involvement common
values.bp: Rare (<30%); mild when present; mucosal scarring NOT a feature — helps distinguish from MMP
values.dh: Rare; no significant mucosal blistering; GI manifestations (bloating, diarrhea) from celiac enteropathy are common but not mucosal blisters

values.pv: Intraepidermal — suprabasilar acantholysis; 'row of tombstones' basal layer; eosinophilic spongiosis may be seen early
values.bp: Subepidermal — clean split at lamina lucida; eosinophilic infiltrate with eosinophils lining the blister floor; neutrophils in early lesions
values.dh: Subepidermal — neutrophil microabscesses at tips of dermal papillae; papillary fibrin deposition; vesicle formation by papillary coalescence

values.pv: Intercellular IgG + C3 throughout epidermis — 'fishnet' or 'honeycomb' pattern; pathognomonic; biopsy from perilesional normal skin
values.bp: Linear IgG + C3 along basement membrane zone (BMZ); salt-split skin: epidermal (roof) pattern — BP is above lamina lucida
values.dh: Granular IgA deposits at tips of dermal papillae — pathognomonic; biopsy from uninvolved skin (not perilesional); IIF on substrate usually negative

values.pv: Desmoglein 3 (Dsg3) — mucosal-dominant; Dsg3 + Dsg1 — mucocutaneous; desmosomal cadherins; ELISA: anti-Dsg3 and/or anti-Dsg1 IgG
values.bp: BP180 (BPAG2, type XVII collagen; NC16A domain most immunogenic) + BP230 (BPAG1; plakin family); hemidesmosomal proteins; ELISA: anti-BP180 + anti-BP230 IgG
values.dh: Tissue transglutaminase (tTG; TG2) IgA — marker of celiac; epidermal transglutaminase (eTG; TG3) IgA — specific to DH skin disease; serum anti-tTG IgA + anti-endomysial IgA positive

values.pv: Rituximab 1 g IV × 2 (D0 + D14) — PEMPHIX trial first-line (PMID 28342530); superior to prednisone monotherapy; ± short-course prednisone bridge
values.bp: Superpotent topical clobetasol propionate 0.05% BID — PMID 11898951; non-inferior to oral prednisone with lower 1-year mortality in elderly; doxycycline 200 mg + niacinamide for mild/frail
values.dh: Dapsone 50–200 mg/day — dramatic response within 72 h is near-pathognomonic; PLUS strict gluten-free diet (GFD) — definitive long-term treatment; check G6PD before starting dapsone

values.pv: HIGH — historically uniformly fatal before systemic steroids (pre-1950s); significant morbidity from superinfection and sepsis; current 5-year mortality ~5–10% in treated patients (PMID 31448731)
values.bp: SIGNIFICANT in elderly — 1-year mortality 20–40% in elderly patients even with treatment, largely from comorbidities and steroid adverse effects; disease itself rarely directly fatal in younger patients (PMID 35538739)
values.dh: LOW disease-specific mortality; persistent quality-of-life impact from pruritus and dietary restriction; untreated celiac enteropathy increases risk of GI lymphoma (EATL); GFD normalizes cancer risk (PMID 35538739)
